question: Most of Ashoka’s edicts were composed in which language?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Prakrit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Most of Ashoka’s edicts** were composed in the **Prakrit language**, which was the common language of the masses during that period.
 
• Prakrit was chosen because it was widely understood by ordinary people across the Mauryan Empire, making it easier to communicate the emperor’s messages.
 
• The edicts were inscribed on rocks and pillars, emphasizing **Dhamma (righteousness)**, moral values, and non-violence.
 
• While Prakrit was the primary language, some edicts were written in other scripts and languages, such as **Greek, Aramaic, and Sanskrit**, to address diverse communities.
 
• These inscriptions were written in the **Brahmi script**, the most prominent script of ancient India, and in some cases, the Kharosthi script was also used.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Prakrit Language:**

 
 
• Prakrit refers to a group of middle Indo-Aryan languages that were spoken in ancient and medieval India.
 
• It was the vernacular language as opposed to Sanskrit, which was considered the language of the elite and scholars.
 
• Examples of Prakrit dialects include **Magadhi, Shauraseni, and Ardhamagadhi**.
 
• It was widely used in Jain and Buddhist texts as well.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka’s Edicts:**
 
 
• The edicts of Emperor Ashoka are a collection of 33 inscriptions found across South Asia, including India, Nepal, Pakistan, and Afghanistan.
 
• They provide valuable historical information about Ashoka’s reign, his policies, and his adoption of Buddhism.
 
• The inscriptions focus on themes like **religious tolerance, welfare of people, animal rights, and ethical conduct**.
 
• They are considered one of the earliest examples of written communication by an Indian ruler.
 
 
 
• **Brahmi Script:**
 
 
• The Brahmi script is one of the oldest writing systems used in the Indian subcontinent and is the precursor to many modern scripts like Devanagari and Tamil.
 
• The script was used extensively in Ashoka’s inscriptions, especially in the **Prakrit language**.
 
• It is written from left to right and is phonetic in nature.
 
 
 
• **Other Languages in Ashoka's Inscriptions:**
 
 
• While Prakrit was the dominant language, some inscriptions in regions like Kandahar were written in **Greek and Aramaic**.
 
• This demonstrates Ashoka’s efforts to communicate with diverse linguistic and cultural groups within his empire.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• Ashoka’s inscriptions are a vital source of information about the **Mauryan Empire**, its administration, and the spread of Buddhism.
 
• They also reflect the emperor’s commitment to ethical governance and his conversion to Buddhism after the Kalinga War.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Languages of the Edicts:**

 
 
• Prakrit was the main language, written in Brahmi script.
 
• Greek and Aramaic were used in Afghanistan and other northwestern regions of the empire.
 
 
 
• **Kalinga War and Ashoka’s Transformation:**
 
 
• The Kalinga War (circa 261 BCE) was a turning point in Ashoka’s life and led to his adoption of Buddhism and the principles of non-violence.
 
• The edicts reflect his efforts to promote **Dhamma** (moral law) across his empire.
 
 
 
• **Key Locations:**
 
 
• Some significant sites of Ashoka’s inscriptions include **Sanchi, Sarnath, Dhauli, and Girnar**.
 
• The Kandahar inscription is notable for being written in Greek and Aramaic.
